introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Information and Communication Technologies 2 (0796), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You will be graded on your ability to use good English, organise information clearly and the use of specialist vocabulary where appropriate. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Computer networks are sometimes classified based on the topology.

(a) What is a network topology? (1 mark)

(b) Use a diagram to describe a star topology of eight nodes with client-server architecture (4 marks)

(c) State two disadvantages of a ring topology compared to a star network. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Network topology (1 mark).** A network topology is the way in which the computers and other devices (the nodes), and the cables or links between them, are arranged and connected in a network (the physical or logical layout of the network).

**(b) Star topology with eight nodes in a client-server architecture (4 marks).** In a star topology every node is connected by its **own cable** to a **central device** (a switch or a hub). With a client-server architecture one of the nodes is the **server**, which stores the shared files and services and answers the requests, and the other nodes are the **clients** (workstations) which send requests to it. With eight nodes, there are 1 server and 7 clients, all around the central switch; all the data between two nodes passes through the switch.

![fig-1](gce-al-ict-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_1.png)

(If the examiner counts eight clients in addition to the server, one more client is added to the same drawing; the structure is the same.)

**(c) Two disadvantages of a ring topology compared with a star (2 marks).**

- In a ring, the data passes through every node, so a break in the cable or the failure of one node can stop the whole network, whereas in a star only the failed node is cut off (the failure of the central switch is the only serious case).
- It is harder to locate a fault and to add or remove a node (the ring must be opened, which interrupts the network), whereas in a star a new node is simply plugged into the switch.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Differentiate the following by describing each component.

(a) Internet and www. (2 marks)

(b) Intranet and extranet. (2 marks)

(c) Browser and search engine. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Internet and WWW (2 marks).**

- The **Internet** is the worldwide network of interconnected computer networks (cables, routers, servers), which communicate with the TCP/IP protocols. It is the infrastructure and it carries many services: e-mail, file transfer, voice calls, and the web.
- The **World Wide Web (WWW)** is only one of those services: a collection of web pages and other documents stored on web servers, linked by hyperlinks, identified by URLs and transferred with the HTTP/HTTPS protocol.

**(b) Intranet and extranet (2 marks).**

- An **intranet** is a private network of one organisation (for example a school) that uses internet technology (web pages, browsers) and can be used only by the members of that organisation, behind a firewall.
- An **extranet** is an extension of the intranet that lets selected outside users (suppliers, partners, parents, customers) reach part of it over the internet with a user name and a password.

**(c) Browser and search engine (2 marks).**

- A **browser** is client software (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge) that sends requests to web servers, receives the web pages and displays them to the user.
- A **search engine** is a web service (Google, Bing) that collects and indexes web pages and, when the user types key words, returns a ranked list of links to pages that match. It is used *through* a browser to find pages.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) State one use of low level programming. (1 mark)

(b) Describe a compiler and give one example you have used. (2 marks)

(c) What does it mean by an unsuccessful compilation of a code? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) One use of low-level programming (1 mark).** Writing programs that control the hardware directly and must be very fast and small, such as device drivers, parts of an operating system and the programs of embedded systems (for example the program of a washing machine or of a microcontroller).

**(b) Compiler (2 marks).** A compiler is a translator program that translates the whole source code written in a high-level language into machine code (an executable file) **in one go, before the program is run**, and lists the errors that it finds. The machine code can then be run many times without the compiler. Example: the **GCC compiler** for the C language (used for instance through Code::Blocks or Dev-C++); other examples are Free Pascal and the Java compiler (javac).

**(c) Unsuccessful compilation (1 mark).** It means that the compiler found one or more errors in the source code (for example syntax errors such as a missing semicolon or an undeclared variable), so it displayed error messages and could not produce the executable program; the programmer must correct the errors and compile again.
